nodes.name: Økokrim (Norway)
nodes.note: Norway's white-collar crime unit. Opened an aggravated-corruption investigation into former PM Thorbjørn Jagland on 5 Feb 2026 ("whether gifts, travel and loans were received in connection with his position") and asked for his Council of Europe immunity to be lifted. Jagland, Terje Rød-Larsen and Mona Juul were later charged (reported Feb 2026). Status as of Feb 2026.

nodes.name: Børge Brende
nodes.note: Norway's foreign minister 2013-17; World Economic Forum president 2017-26. Three business dinners with Epstein (2018, at Terje Rød-Larsen's invitation, and twice in 2019) and a few emails and texts; says he did not know his past. Resigned 26 Feb 2026 after a WEF review he requested found no further concerns. No police case reported.

nodes.name: World Economic Forum
nodes.note: Ran an outside-counsel review of its president's Epstein contacts in Feb 2026; co-chairs Hoffmann and Fink said it found nothing beyond what he had disclosed.

nodes.name: Polish government task force (Feb 2026)
nodes.note: Set up by PM Donald Tusk on 3 Feb 2026 under the justice minister: to find whether Polish girls or women were harmed and to examine claims that Epstein was involved with or used by Russian intelligence. No findings published on the intelligence question.

nodes.name: Polish National Prosecutor's Office
nodes.note: Opened a full investigation on 11 Mar 2026 into suspected trafficking by an Epstein-linked group that recruited girls and women in Poland for sexual exploitation, 2009-19, under the pretence of modelling; names Daniel Siad's 2009 email about recruiting in Kraków. A potential suspect identified; no charges.

nodes.name: Keir Starmer
nodes.note: UK prime minister. Appointed Peter Mandelson ambassador to the United States and dismissed him in September 2025 over his Epstein links.

nodes.name: Morgan McSweeney
nodes.note: Starmer's chief of staff. Resigned on 8 Feb 2026, saying the decision to appoint Mandelson was wrong and that he had advised it.
